title: William IX of Montpellier
summary: This document provides a biographical overview of William IX of Montpellier, the last lord of Montpellier from the Guilhem lineage, who ruled from 1202 to 1204. It covers his family background as the eldest son of William VIII and Agnes (his father's second wife, related to the kings of Aragon), and details the controversy surrounding the legitimacy of his parents' marriage, which displaced his half-sister Mary, the original heiress. The document describes William's succession to the lordship in 1202 according to his father's will, his governance featuring the newly created Council of Fifteen, and his subsequent downfall in 1204 when Mary's marriage to King Peter II of Aragon led the townspeople to rebel and expel him in favor of Peter and Mary. Finally, it discusses the papal litigation of 1212–13, in which Pope Innocent III ruled in favor of Peter and Mary while declaring William IX illegitimate due to his father's marriage to Agnes being deemed adulterous.
